Therapy that fits your life, evidence that guides it.

I’m {{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}} offering focused psychotherapy for anxiety, trauma, relationships, and transitions. I work with long-term membership plans and time-limited packages to match clinical needs and life constraints.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} Learn about my approach

Sessions available in-person in {{CITY}}, {{STATE}} and via secure telehealth. Confidentiality and privacy maintained; see full notice in the footer.

{{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}
Private practice therapist · {{MODALITIES}}

Myths people often tell themselves about therapy

A scientist’s guide to what therapy is — and isn’t.

Myth: Therapy will fix me instantly

Therapy is rarely instantaneous. It’s a collaborative process informed by research and tailored to your goals. Progress can be steady but nonlinear.

Truth: Lasting change takes consistent, guided work

I use evidence-based practices and regular review of goals so we can measure what helps and adjust treatment as needed.

Myth: You have to talk about everything right away

There’s no pressure to disclose everything. Safety, pacing, and consent guide what we explore and when.

Truth: We set boundaries and pace together

We’ll co-create a plan that balances immediate coping strategies with deeper therapeutic work when you’re ready.

Three pillars of my practice

A clear framework to understand how we work.

Evidence-guided interventions

I draw on CBT, EMDR-informed strategies, and relational approaches depending on what the client, evidence, and context call for.

Collaborative measurement

We track symptoms and functioning, review progress regularly, and alter course when a strategy isn’t helping.

Clear boundaries & confidentiality

Informed consent, documentation limits, and secure telehealth are standard. I’ll explain what confidentiality covers and where limits apply.

Illustrative cases (anonymized)

Short descriptions of common therapeutic pathways to show how work unfolds.

Reclaiming routine after burnout

Client came with exhaustion and cynicism after years of overwork. We focused on activity scheduling, boundary-setting, and values-aligned planning. Over three months, they reported improved sleep and gradual re-engagement with meaningful activity.

Navigating a relationship transition

One partner sought support managing grief and practical decisions after separation. Work included emotion regulation, communication strategies, and safety planning where needed.

Addressing long-standing anxiety

Through psychoeducation, exposure-informed practice, and attention to avoidance patterns, the client experienced reduced panic frequency and more flexibility in daily life.

All examples are composite and anonymized to protect client privacy and adhere to confidentiality obligations.

Questions I often get

How do membership plans work?

I offer ongoing membership plans that include a sliding number of sessions per month, messaging support during business hours, and periodic outcome reviews. Memberships provide continuity and priority scheduling without making clinical decisions for you.

What if I’m in crisis?

This practice does not provide emergency services. If you are at immediate risk of harming yourself or others, call 911 or go to your nearest emergency department. In the U.S. you can also call 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

Do you accept insurance?

I operate primarily on a private-pay basis and provide superbills to submit to insurance when applicable. We discuss fees and payment during intake so there are no surprises.

Ongoing care plans for steady progress

If you’re looking for continuity, the "Care Membership" offers scheduled sessions, urgent check-ins during business hours, and quarterly progress consultations. Flexible cancellation policies and transparent billing.
